review_output.summary: The new code scrolls the page and then clicks at the original (x, y). Mouse coordinates are relative to the viewport, so after the scroll the click lands on a different element.
review_output.failure_scenario: The coordinates come from GetElementPositionByNameAction's boundingBox(), which is viewport-relative. Take an element at viewport (300, 700) in a 1280x720 viewport. scrollY becomes 700-360=340, the page moves up 340px, and mouse().click(300, 700) hits whatever now sits at that spot, not the target. Any element below the viewport midpoint (or right of the horizontal midpoint) is mis-clicked. The click should go to (x - actualScrollX, y - actualScrollY), or the scroll should be dropped.

review_output.summary: afterWindowHandles comes from Stream.toList(), which returns an unmodifiable list. Calling removeAll on it throws UnsupportedOperationException whenever a click opens a new tab.
review_output.failure_scenario: Clicking a target=_blank link makes pages().size() grow, so the branch runs. afterWindowHandles.removeAll(...) throws UnsupportedOperationException outside the try/catch, and the action fails exactly when new-tab detection is supposed to work.

review_output.summary: In debug mode, removing the marker runs a page.evaluate after the click inside the same try. If the click triggers navigation, that evaluate throws and the action reports failure even though the click worked.
review_output.failure_scenario: With browser.debug=true, a click on a link navigates the page. The evaluate then fails with 'Execution context was destroyed', the catch returns 'Failed to click at position', and the agent retries or gives up on a click that actually succeeded. The cleanup should run in its own try or a finally block.

review_output.summary: The debug marker uses position:absolute at document coordinates (x, y), while x/y are viewport coordinates and the page has just been scrolled. The dot is also removed right after the click, so it is never visible in any screenshot.
review_output.failure_scenario: After scrolling by (scrollX, scrollY), the dot is drawn at document (x, y), which is offset from the actual click point by the scroll amount. It is then removed synchronously, so debug mode gives no useful visual feedback. GetElementPositionByNameAction already uses position:fixed with a setTimeout removal.

review_output.summary: page.viewportSize() returns null when the context has no fixed viewport. The code dereferences it without a check, so every move_to_and_click fails.
review_output.failure_scenario: If the browser context is created with setViewportSize(null) or noViewport, viewportSize().width throws NullPointerException. The catch turns that into 'Failed to click' every time, a regression from the old code, which did not need the viewport.

review_output.summary: getBrowserDebug() returns a nullable Boolean, and assigning it to a primitive boolean unboxes it. The getter is now called before the try block on every click.
review_output.failure_scenario: If the manus.browser.debug config row is missing (configService returns null) and the field was never initialised, unboxing throws NullPointerException. execute() then fails for every move_to_and_click, and before this change it did not depend on that setting at all.

review_output.summary: The auto-prefix check is case-sensitive and only knows http/https, so it breaks every other URL scheme and mixed-case input.
review_output.failure_scenario: about:blank, file:///tmp/a.html, data:text/html,..., chrome://settings and 'HTTP://example.com' all get 'https://' prepended (e.g. 'https://about:blank', 'https://HTTP://example.com'), so navigation fails. 'localhost:8080' becomes https://localhost:8080 and fails against a plain-HTTP dev server. The check should test for any scheme (e.g. the regex ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*:) and only add a prefix when none is present.

review_output.summary: Changing null to " " only hides the real bug. The condition should use && rather than ||, and the merged prompt is computed but never saved.
review_output.failure_scenario: With the new " " default, getSystemPrompt() is never null, so the block runs on every update and logs the 'deprecated SystemPrompt' warning each time. A null value still NPEs on trim(). For a legacy agent with a real systemPrompt, the merged nextPrompt is discarded: updateEntityFromConfig then overwrites nextStepPrompt, so the old system prompt is silently lost. The fix is `!= null && !trim().isEmpty()` plus actually storing the merged value.

review_output.summary: pressSequentially with a fixed 100ms delay per character runs under Playwright's default 30s action timeout. Long text times out partway and has to fall back, and keystrokes already typed (such as Enter) have already fired.
review_output.failure_scenario: Any text over about 300 characters times out after 30s of typing, so the call blocks for 30s and then falls back to fill(). If the text contains '\n', Enter presses during the partial typing can submit the form before the fallback clears and refills the field. The JS fallback sets el.value directly, which React/Vue controlled inputs ignore, and fires no 'change' event.

review_output.summary: ElementHandle, Random and WaitForSelectorState are now unused imports. The step comments are also wrong: '3. 尝试 fill' sits above pressSequentially and '4. fill 失败，尝试 pressSequentially' sits above fill.
review_output.failure_scenario: The dead imports can fail style or lint checks, and the swapped comments describe the opposite of what the code does, which misleads maintainers. The fallback chain also partly repeats the existing InteractiveElementRegistry.fillText helper.
